report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. The Kyleena levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (19.5 mg) is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years.

### Supporting Evidence

1. **FDA Indication & Approval:** The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Bayer’s Kyleena in September 2016. The official FDA-approved prescribing information specifies that Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years, after which the device should be removed or replaced if continued contraception is needed.
2. **Clinical Trial Efficacy:** Approval was supported by a Phase III clinical study involving 1,452 women aged 18 to 35. Over the 5-year evaluation period, Kyleena demonstrated high contraceptive efficacy, with a 1-year Pearl Index of 0.16 and a cumulative 5-year Pearl Index of 0.29 (yielding over 99% effectiveness for each year of use).
3. **Hormonal Release Rate:** Kyleena initially releases levonorgestrel at approximately 17.5 mcg/day at 24 days post-insertion, which gradually declines to 9.8 mcg/day after one year and continues decreasing over time. Five years represents the validated maximum period for reliable efficacy under its current label.

* **Kyleena Official Prescribing Information:** https://www.kyleena-us.com/prescribing-information
* **FDA Drug Label Summary:** https://medlibrary.org/lib/rx/meds/kyleena/
* **Bayer Prescribing & Clinical Efficacy Data:** https://www.bayer.com/sites/default/files/KYLEENA_EN_PI.pdf
